correctness.rationale: Invertibility is detected modulo the radical. A commuting residue partner of a nonscalar lift is a polynomial of degree at most one in the residue matrix and lifts by lifting the coefficients; the remaining choices form a 2d-dimensional kernel. For a scalar reduction the simultaneous commutant of the radical coefficients controls all lifts, with fiber size q^{4d}. A nonscalar 2×2 coefficient generates its two-dimensional commutant. Distinct such algebras meet only in scalars; a noncommuting pair has scalar common commutant. This gives the five scalar-lift rows by counting coefficient tuples and the three nonscalar rows by field conjugacy types, also when q=2 or d=1. Weighting by centralizer order divided by |G| gives the class count. The exceptional row contributes D/[q(q+1)] classes; its exact complement is q^{2d+2}−q^d, so dominance is asymptotic at fixed q, not asserted at every d≥2. The argument does not require a coefficient field. Independent bounded arithmetic (python3 /workspace/independent_arithmetic_checks.py) checked totals, weighted orbit counts and the complement for 48 parameter pairs. The frozen checker and its recorded five small-ring runs are corroboration only and were not executed.

evidence: The full-ring result has q^{2d} lifts per commuting residue partner at nonscalar reduction and q^{4d} per scalar-lift commutant partner. For a nonscalar residue the algebra is k[A]; for scalar reduction it is either M₂(k), one of the regular quadratic algebras, or kI. Each regular algebra contributes q^{2d}−q^d tuples; the scalar residual case is exactly D.
Its §4 proves the commuting-pair lift weights q^{8d} for scalar-scalar and q^{6d} for all other commuting residue pairs.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The unit orders of the three standard quadratic algebras k×k, F_{q²}, and k[t]/(t²) are (q−1)², q²−1, q(q−1). Split the regular algebras by the standard counts q(q+1)/2 (unordered eigenline pairs), q(q−1)/2 (quadratic field normalizer index), q+1 (nilpotent image lines); then restrict the q scalar residues to q−1 choices. This gives the five scalar-reduction rows, including the same D. For nonscalar reductions, standard GL₂(k) rational canonical types give the exact M_s,M_i,M_j populations; multiply by the known q^{4d} lift count and the known centralizer fiber size q^{2d}. For K, use the known lift weights but replace the total and scalar-scalar residue-pair counts by U(q²−1) and (q−1)²; dividing by Uq^{4d} gives the frozen formula. Dividing the already counted exceptional population by its class size and subtracting from K gives the complement and share. This is a unit restriction and standard field-type refinement of the established census, not a new square-zero classification.
